approach.method_basis: The Parent trains a recurrent SMILES language model on an unlabeled molecular corpus and starts each objective with a policy copied from its frozen prior. It learns from the highest-scoring half of each accepted batch and the strongest eligible historical records in a memory of thirty-two elites. Original accepted strings and rewards are retained. Historical fitting weights diminish with previous exposure, while total current and historical loss shares stay fixed. Targets are prior sequence log likelihood plus sixty times reward, with individually positive targets capped at zero. Up to twelve clipped Adam steps minimize weighted squared residuals, retaining the final policy. Complete strings are sampled directly from that policy; RDKit validity and canonical novelty checks admit the first eligible molecules and refill the announced batch.
approach.novelty: Add one electronic-state admission rule: a sampled molecule must have zero RDKit-assigned radical electrons. A positive count redirects its slot to another fresh policy draw without editing atoms, charges, bonds or the sampled serialization. The earlier sampling child spaced repeated cores and lost endpoint score; this rule places no penalty on repeated cores. Earlier chemical gates in other lineages constrained sulfur environments or halogen attachments. This predicate instead checks the assigned unpaired-electron count on every element, leaving closed-shell charged species and ordinary sulfur chemistry eligible. The Parent's six observed cases establish a small but real opportunity. The claim is cleaner admitted electronic states with score non-inferiority, not a predicted endpoint increase.

hypothesis: Admit a complete, valid, canonically novel direct-policy sample only when the parsed canonical identity has zero RDKit-assigned radical electrons; reject positive-radical candidates before emission and refill from fresh policy draws.

finding_summary.headline: Radical-bearing emissions fell to zero, but six replacements failed score non-inferiority.
finding_summary.insights:
Rare admission changes can matter even when the excluded parent molecules were poor and never selected for training. All eleven sessions without an open-capacity gate intervention reproduced the complete parent molecular and score sequence. Every affected session preserved its matched proposal prefix until the first rejection. One affected deco_hop session changed only two batches’ admissions and ordering: its selected training records and audited training quantities remained exactly equal throughout. In two other sessions, replacements entered the unchanged elite-selection rule, giving a direct route into later feedback. The same immediate chemical exclusion can therefore leave learning unchanged or alter it, depending on what fills the slot.

The largest loss followed a replacement that never trained. In its first affected zaleplon_mpo update, the ten selected training records, rewards and targets were identical to the parent, but the inherited padding width shrank from 72 to 60 tokens because it is set using the larger batch, including unselected strings. Tiny recorded update differences appeared immediately; a further proposal difference appeared in batch five, followed by broad trajectory divergence. This exposes a route for an unselected molecule to affect numerical execution and makes numerical sensitivity a plausible contributor to the loss. The logs do not isolate a hardware arithmetic cause or show that the radical-bearing chemical feature itself was useful. The evidence rules out treating “never elite” as sufficient assurance that rejection will preserve the later search.

The molecular assessment helps explain what this narrow predicate leaves open. The main losing trajectory explored many more long hydrocarbon appendages and failed to recover its parent’s compact heteroaryl-ether amide endpoint, whereas the improving trajectory favored less overdecorated anilinoquinazolines. These are observed chemical associations, not proof of a causal feature. Ring-rich exploration remains broad, while undefined stereochemistry, reactive closed-shell handles and uncontrolled appendage growth persist. Zero RDKit radical electrons therefore establishes the intended representation constraint, not general medicinal quality or stability. Future attempts would need to resolve replacement usefulness and sensitivity to batch representation; the present result does not support a score-safe blanket exclusion or a reduction in raw generation of unusual states.
finding_summary.results:
The electronic-state gate executed correctly. Across all three seeds and five tasks, it rejected six valid, novel, positive-radical draws while capacity was open and delivered six newly drawn closed-shell replacements. Those interventions occurred in six of 435 batches, spanning four task/seed sessions. Emitted positive-radical occurrence fell from the parent’s six in 4,350 proposals to zero in 4,350; the passive first-come comparator on the child’s actual stream also contained six. All 4,350 eligible zero-radical rows passed, including 315 charged molecules and 1,058 sulfur-containing molecules. Seventeen positive-radical raw-valid draws still occurred: six were rejected and eleven arrived after capacity was full. Thus admission changed; reduced raw radical generation has not been established. All 15 sessions completed their 300-evaluation budgets.

The promised score non-inferiority was rejected. Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.522705 to 0.516739, a paired change of −0.005966, exceeding the allowed 0.002 loss. Seeds 0 and 1 were unchanged; seed 2 lost 0.017898 in macro score. In that seed, zaleplon_mpo fell from 0.500000 to 0.391286, outweighing deco_hop’s rise from 0.666949 to 0.686174; the other three endpoints were unchanged. Population seed SD was 0.011993 versus 0.020072, and recorded mean AUC fell from 0.405593 to 0.404156. None of the six immediate replacements improved an incumbent; two entered subsequent real training. Total suggestion time rose from 24.745 to 31.427 seconds, including 6.185 seconds of inspection and 0.792 seconds in receipt regions. These are recorded regions, not isolated estimates of causal overhead.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich medicinal scaffolds with closed-shell atom assignments, but undefined stereochemistry, fragile handles and uneven appendage growth.
molecular.overall_character: The complete seeds 0, 1 and 2 were read for every objective in the supplied order; tasks_without_trajectories is empty. Each task contributes 900 accepted records, including 870 optimizer appearances. The digest initial excerpt shows seed 0 and its final excerpt shows seed 2; those excerpts are not the whole seed panel. All Child and Parent trajectory files were inspected passively. Across 4,350 Child optimizer appearances, RDKit 2023.09.6 perceives a median of 26 heavy atoms and three rings, with a heavy-atom range of 4 to 90. The digest ring-closure rates run from 0.9805 to 0.9977 and aromatic-text occurrence rates from 0.9460 to 0.9966; these are fractions of SMILES containing those features, not fractions of atoms that are aromatic. Aromatic amides, quinazolines, piperazines and other cyclic amines, sulfones/sulfonamides, ethers and halogenated aryl groups are prominent. Nonaromatic rings occur in 1,841 appearances, so this is not exclusively flat aromatic chemistry. The medicinal motifs make many individual structures apparently makeable, but the whole output also contains overgrown chains, repeated polar groups and reactive or form-sensitive attachments. That supports questionable synthetic plausibility and moderate drug-likeness for the collection, without asserting a synthetic route or experimental property. The 2,811 distinct nonempty atom/bond-typed Murcko cores indicate broad overall graph exploration; enrichment of the strongest molecules in narrower families remains visible. Core counts retain linker and heteroatom distinctions and do not measure diversity of biological activity. The Child has zero positive RDKit radical-electron assignments versus six Parent appearances, while 315 Child appearances contain formal atomic charges and 1,058 contain sulfur. This is a molecular-representation observation only. All tasks have a stereocentre-text rate of 0.0; passive perception nevertheless finds 870 Child appearances with at least one unassigned carbon stereocentre, and no explicit tetrahedral or bond-stereochemical text. Eleven complete task/seed molecular-score sequences match the Parent exactly; four differ, with unchanged endpoint identities in two of those. No mechanism-activation or score-utility decision is made. The reproducible passive counts, digest-to-trajectory checks, file hashes and per-seed comparisons are in r0012-08-improve-L03-molecular.audit.py and r0012-08-improve-L03-molecular.audit.json beside this report.

per_task.generated_character: Mostly medium-sized aromatic amides: optimizer heavy atoms have median 24 and range 4-90, with median three rings. The ring/aromatic text rates are 0.9908/0.9839. The strongest digest structure, O=C(NCc1ccccn1)c1cccc(Cn2ccccc2=O)c1, is a three-ring benzamide joining a pyridylmethyl group and an N-substituted pyridone. Other strong molecules include acetamido-indole carboxamides, anilinopyridine carboxamides, sulfinamides and an O-benzyl hydroxamate. These are recognizable medicinal motifs, although their exact molecular forms and synthesis have not been demonstrated. Seed 0 retains the indole-amide endpoint at 0.43351949803907636 and seed 1 the pyridone-containing benzamide at 0.4767312946227961. Both full streams match the Parent. Seed 2 ends with a best value of 0.39128611874634317 in a substituted diarylamide/urea family, whereas the Parent reached 0.5 with a compact heteroaryl-ether carboxanilide. That Parent structure is described from its trajectory rather than quoted because it is absent from this digest. The Child contains a much larger long-chain tail: 15 optimizer strings have an uninterrupted C run of at least 10, versus one in the Parent.
liabilities: Long hydrocarbon tails inflate size and flexibility; the worst set includes a very long-chain sulfonium species as well as long neutral amides. Closed-shell atom assignments do not resolve these liabilities.

The high-scoring sulfinamide/imidic-acid representations and hydroxamate show unresolved form-sensitive chemistry. Their presence is not evidence that all such bonds are unstable or synthetically inaccessible.
missing_features: Reliable retention of compact aryl/heteroaryl carbonyl arrangements during appendage changes is missing from much of the stream, especially the seed-2 long-chain excursion. The examples do not identify a unique absent target scaffold.

Defined configurations are missing for eligible stereogenic variants: 118 optimizer appearances have an unassigned carbon centre. Their scores do not establish that configuration assignment alone would improve this objective.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The observed gradient favors compact, organized aromatic carbonyl/heteroatom arrangements over indiscriminate chain growth. The best benzamide scores 0.4767312946227961; adding the digest phenol substituent gives 0.44383095403034933, so additional hydrogen-bond functionality is not automatically rewarded. The final decanoyl diarylamide scores 0.000005647693002104746, while the neighboring shorter branched-acyl analogues score 0.34072682485201594 and 0.34977917230128097; the halogen differences make these associations rather than a fully controlled series. The extremely long-chain amides in the worst excerpt score 0.0. The O-benzyl hydroxamate still reaches 0.4629100498862757 and the sulfinamide 0.4531317717091581, so the evidence does not justify removing every N-O bond or sulfur-containing group. The digest median is 0.076866.

per_task.generated_character: This panel is especially aromatic and heavily decorated: median 32 heavy atoms, median four rings, and ring/aromatic text rates 0.9977/0.9966. Halogens occur in 0.7207 of optimizer SMILES. All twelve best digest entries are seed-2 anilinoquinazoline analogues with methoxy groups, fluorinated phenyl substituents and variable alkyl, alkoxy, amino, nitrile or extra aryl appendages. These cores are apparently plausible medicinal chemistry, with substantial flat aromatic surface. The full other seeds also sample different nitrogen-rich aromatic and hydrazone families. Seed-0 and seed-1 recorded endpoints remain 0.5998615059406662 and 0.6263699396108253 with their Parent endpoint identities. Seed 2 reaches 0.6861742139310967 versus the Parent 0.6669492630755185. Its endpoint has 28 heavy atoms and three aromatic rings, whereas the Parent endpoint, also present in the Child digest, has 35 heavy atoms and four aromatic rings. Across the task, 353 distinct typed Murcko cores versus the Parent 355 show substantial exploration despite concentration among the best examples.
liabilities: Large aromatic surfaces and frequent halogens can create a solubility and lipophilicity burden; those properties were not measured here. The 90-heavy-atom extreme shows that overgrowth remains possible.
N-rich imine/hydrazone and other reactive-handle chemistry persists in the broader stream. Familiar ring systems and nonradical assignments alone do not establish a stable, tractable molecular form.
missing_features: The best excerpt does not demonstrate comparable success after replacing the anilinoquinazoline architecture with another ring topology; most of its high-score variation is decoration of that family. Broader raw core availability already exists.

The output lacks consistent control of appendage size and aromatic surface while keeping its useful heteroatom arrangement. No exact unobserved scaffold or pharmacophore can be inferred from this score landscape.
Explicit configurations are absent from the 103 appearances with perceived unassigned carbon stereocentres; the strongest pentan-3-yl example itself has no such carbon centre.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The trajectory supports anilino-fused diazine geometry with tuned peripheral decoration. CCC(CC)c1cc2c(Nc3ccc(F)c(F)c3)ncnc2c(OC)c1OC scores 0.6861742139310967; its trifluorophenyl analogue scores 0.6856617647058824. Adding a phenyl group to the latter core lowers the recorded value to 0.6695813460519343. The corresponding difluoro butoxy pair gives 0.6840559232542575 without the extra phenyl and 0.6666996765035981 with it. These close structural comparisons support restraint in aryl growth within this family, not a universal smaller-is-better rule. In contrast, the worst diaryl-quinoline sulfone/acid scores 0.28535067873303166 and an indole aryl ketone/sulfone scores 0.28799019607843135. Small dichlorostyrene and methyl isothiocyanate remain near 0.5, which also warns against reading that baseline as medicinal quality. The digest median is 0.5748.

per_task.generated_character: The strongest molecules combine several aryl surfaces with unacylated cyclic amines and alkyl linkers. Median size is 28 heavy atoms and three rings; ring/aromatic text rates are 0.9874/0.969. Seed 0 emphasizes aryl/benzyl piperazines, seed 1 benzofused cyclic amines and arylpiperazines connected to benzyl phenol/anisole groups, and seed 2 aryl ketones carrying a propoxy-piperidine appendage. In contrast with an absence-of-basic-nitrogen diagnosis, 490 optimizer appearances have an unacylated saturated ring-nitrogen structural proxy. The common amine, aryl and ketone/ether motifs are apparently makeable, although large flexible compounds and unusual side chains remain. All three complete molecular-score streams match the Parent. Their recorded endpoint values are 0.9999997933663268, 0.9999997851052089 and 0.9999991526291698.
liabilities: The O-CH2-Cl group is an electrophilic, potentially labile attachment rather than an ordinary aryl chloride. It occurs in four emitted appearances and remains present in a near-ceiling digest example.

Several strong molecules have long flexible linkers, multiple potentially protonatable amines and substantial hydrophobic aryl surface. Their SMILES are mostly formally neutral; that is not evidence that they remain neutral in solution.
missing_features: What is uneven is preservation of the favorable cyclic-amine/aryl attachment relationship, not availability of cyclic amines. Much of the lower-score stream acylates or sulfonylates nitrogen or changes that relationship.
Conservative attachment chemistry is missing even among the best-scoring molecules, as the chloromethyl ether demonstrates. Near-ceiling scores do not establish a stable medicinal form.
Stereochemical definition is absent for 190 appearances with perceived unassigned carbon centres. The cited endpoint structures do not require treating every molecule as tetrahedrally stereogenic.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best aryl/benzyl piperazine scores 0.9999997933663268, and the benzofused cyclic-amine/benzyl-phenol compound 0.9999997851052089. Poorer molecules often place nitrogen in amide or sulfonamide environments or fail to present the same amine/aryl relationship: the N-acylated piperidine carboxamide scores 0.000026715842904959654 and the sulfonyl-piperidine heteroaryl amide 0.000019828327575562915. The final structure retaining the propoxy-piperidine arm scores 0.999988872643426, whereas a smaller amino ketone without that arm scores 0.0035116287191461495; these also differ in linker constitution, so the arm is an association rather than an isolated causal feature. A longer ether/amide linker gives 0.5728095677025575, while multiple ordinary alkyl linker lengths are already close to the ceiling. Crucially, the chloromethyl-ether-bearing arylpiperazine still scores 0.9999994163676008. The reported score therefore does not itself screen out that reactive attachment. The digest median is 0.049032.

per_task.generated_character: Medium-sized, varied heterocyclic chemistry has median 24 heavy atoms and three rings, with ring/aromatic text rates 0.9908/0.9632. Piperazines, aryl sulfonamides, quinoline-like fused aromatics, benzodioxoles, ethers and lactam/carbonyl groups recur. The strongest digest molecule joins a methylquinoline sulfonyl group and a benzodioxole sulfonyl group across piperazine; its five perceived rings include three aromatic rings. Both piperazine nitrogens are sulfonylated, so calling this molecule a free basic piperazine would be wrong. Many conventional sulfonamide/piperazine connections look synthetically plausible, while the N-rich unsaturated ring and form-sensitive outliers require individual assessment. The task retains 732 typed Murcko cores, the same as the Parent. All three endpoint identities and values remain unchanged: 0.2125118592516207, 0.20428349275442803 and 0.2588686674995393; only the late seed-2 molecular sequence differs.
liabilities: Sulfonamide multiplication changes nitrogen basicity and adds substantial polar functionality. It can coexist with the best observed score here, so the concern must be evaluated in molecular context.

Azide, N-O-bearing and form-sensitive N-rich fragments remain among poorer molecules. The tiny fragments and long hydrophobic charged species are chemically unlike the better organized multi-ring compounds.
missing_features: The stream does not reliably assemble complementary ring and aryl-linker features into the organized arrangements found among its strongest molecules. Hundreds of distinct cores already exist, so a simple claim of missing ring diversity is unsupported.
No unique absent reference scaffold can be diagnosed from these modest scores. The supported gap is productive attachment organization rather than a prescribed nitrogen charge state.
The 187 optimizer appearances with unassigned carbon stereocentres lack explicit configuration, without evidence here of which configuration would help.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Organized combinations of cyclic nitrogen and aryl/sulfonyl anchors outperform isolated small polar or reactive fragments. The bis-sulfonyl piperazine scores 0.2588686674995393, compared with 0.2272296156064184 for the related quinoline-sulfonyl N-methylpiperazine. An N-methylpiperazine joined through an aminoethyl sulfonamide to benzodioxole scores 0.2229480268629566, so alternative attachment arrangements can also be useful. A simpler N-methylpiperazine/pyrrolylmethyl final molecule scores 0.13091966785799863: having the ring alone is insufficient. The small alkyl azide scores 0.0, sulfamic acid 0.02668612498071339, and the small sulfur-linked diacid 0.02095188685475281. Sulfur and polarity are therefore context-dependent, and the best structure explicitly contradicts a universal demand for an unsulfonylated basic nitrogen. The digest median is 0.127565.

per_task.generated_character: This is a broad mixture rather than convergence on one scaffold: median 24 heavy atoms, median three rings, and 774 distinct typed Murcko cores. Ring/aromatic text rates are 0.9805/0.9460. The top seed-2 structure is a single fluorinated/trifluoromethyl phenyl ring bearing an N-acylsulfonamide and a butyl-substituted secondary aminoacetyl arm. Other strong molecules include branched oxalamides, aryl-sulfonyl imidazolines with an ester, a guanidino benzofused N ring, and a quinolinone-linked thiourea/thiophene assembly. Conventional amide and sulfonamide connections appear makeable, but the full set also includes overgrown peptide-like chains, lipid-like tails and complicated tautomer-sensitive heterocycles. All three complete streams match the Parent exactly. Seed endpoints remain 0.2711448282680827, 0.26424211308214746 and 0.32609684308650033. The digest median displays 0.0; this rounded display is not evidence that half the exact scores equal zero.
liabilities: Long aliphatic tails and repeated amide/carbonyl growth produce large flexible or strongly polar outliers. These are present despite ring-rich chemistry elsewhere in the same stream.

Several structures combine acidic and basic groups or tautomer-sensitive C=N/C=S chemistry. Such structures require contextual form assessment; the absence of an assigned radical is insufficient to establish stability or synthetic feasibility.
missing_features: The generator lacks consistent compact organization of polar functions and aryl substituents across its proposals. The highest-scoring features appear intermittently while larger peptide-like and heteroatom-heavy combinations remain common possibilities.

Explicit stereochemical choices are missing for the branched oxalamide, the guanidino benzofused-ring example and other eligible structures. Passive perception finds 272 optimizer appearances with an unassigned carbon centre; no stereoisomer comparison was evaluated here.

Uniformly coherent ionization and tautomeric presentation is not demonstrated across amino N-acylsulfonamides, guanidines, imidates and thioureas. The observed scores alone do not identify a preferred solution-state form.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Compact placement of carbonyl/nitrogen groups with suitable aryl substitution is associated with the best observed values. CCCCNCC(=O)NS(=O)(=O)c1cc(C(F)(F)F)ccc1F scores 0.32609684308650033, and the branched fluorinated oxalamide 0.3085499097640706. In a close aryl-sulfonyl imidazoline pair, the fluorophenyl compound scores 0.3034617343186778 versus 0.24905607529893223 without that fluorine. Replacing the ester by its imidate representation in the fluorinated example gives 0.2795168707513844. By contrast, the long peptide-like and lipid-like digest structures score 0.0; another heavily carbonylated and nitrogen-rich structure scores 3.540513082254524e-90. The final repeated-carbonyl heterocycle scores 2.6445959326166367e-17. Neither adding more polar groups nor simply adding amines and rings is sufficient. Because several unrelated compact families score better, these records do not reveal a unique missing target pharmacophore.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every task has a digest stereocentre-text rate of 0.0. Passive RDKit perception finds an unassigned carbon stereocentre in 870 of 4,350 optimizer appearances, with no assigned centres or explicit bond-stereochemical text. The digest oxalamide CCC(CC(=O)Nc1cc(C(F)(F)F)ccc1F)NC(=O)C(=O)N(C)C contains a carbon centre whose configuration is unspecified. Many other leading structures are achiral, so the gap applies only where the graph supports stereochemistry.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not explicitly specify configurations for the stereogenic structures it emits.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator would need to recognize eligible stereogenic elements and generate explicit configurations while preserving connectivity and useful attachment relationships. Configuration coverage should be demonstrated on actual emitted identities; these records do not establish a score benefit for any stereoisomer.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The digest includes zero-scoring long-chain amides and peptide-like repeats. CCCCCCCCCC(=O)Nc1ccc(C(=O)Nc2cccc(F)c2)cc1 scores 0.000005647693002104746, whereas its shorter branched-acyl relatives score much higher. Conversely, useful molecules already include ordinary extended alkyl linkers. The full proposal panel spans 4-90 heavy atoms; extreme size is an observed output property, not a required property of its better structures.
transferable_gaps.gap: Appendage growth is not reliably coordinated with the existing scaffold and polar-group load.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The generator needs scaffold-context-dependent control of linker length, substituent extent and repeated polar functions while retaining learned attachment patterns. This evidence supports coherent growth from observed feedback, not a universal preference for short, nonpolar or minimally substituted molecules.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Strong emitted families include unacylated aryl/benzyl piperazines and linked cyclic amines, while a ring-N-acylated piperidine carboxamide is near the low end of its own observed score span. Yet Cc1cc(S(=O)(=O)N2CCN(S(=O)(=O)c3ccc4c(c3)OCO4)CC2)c2ccccc2n1 is the strongest molecule in another supplied span even though both piperazine nitrogens are sulfonylated. The full output already contains 1,003 appearances of an unacylated saturated ring-nitrogen proxy; there is no general absence of that chemistry.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve the chemical role of ring nitrogen when it changes attachments.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The generator needs to distinguish amine, amide, sulfonamide and conjugated nitrogen attachment contexts while exploring new structures. Preserve or deliberately vary the role learned from accepted molecules instead of treating nitrogen count, ring presence or a universally basic piperazine as the objective.

transferable_gaps.evidence: All 4,350 emitted optimizer appearances have zero RDKit-assigned radical electrons, but Fc1ccc(N2CCN(CCCCNCc3ccc(OCCl)cc3)CC2)cc1F still scores 0.9999994163676008 and contains a chloromethyl ether. O=S(Nc1cc(C(O)=NCc2ccccc2Cl)ccn1)c1ccccc1 retains imidic-acid/sulfinamide form sensitivity at 0.42730032301881693. Other strong molecules contain ordinary sulfur chemistry or an N-O linkage, so a blanket heteroatom or bond ban would discard chemistry already associated with good observed values.
transferable_gaps.gap: Closed-shell atom assignments leave reactive attachment chemistry and uncertain molecular forms unresolved.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The generator needs context-aware treatment of electrophilic attachments and tautomer/ionization forms beyond parse validity and radical count. Any future change should distinguish a specific molecular-form concern from ordinary aryl halides, charges, sulfur or N-O chemistry, without equating a structural filter with demonstrated experimental stability.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The output has 2,811 nonempty atom/bond-typed Murcko cores, but all twelve highest entries in one digest are decorated anilinoquinazolines from a single seed. Another panel has 732 distinct typed cores while its strongest structure is an organized bis-sulfonyl piperazine. Thus neither complete scaffold collapse nor a general lack of rings explains the remaining chemistry; many different graphs are available but useful combinations are uneven.
transferable_gaps.gap: Broad graph novelty has not established reliable diversification of the attachment patterns in the strongest families.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The generator needs to explore altered ring topology, saturation and substituent vectors while retaining the functional-group relationships supported by its own accepted molecules. Evidence should track actual productive structural families, since additional canonical identities or core counts alone do not establish better chemistry.

method_name: Augmented Hill-Climb with a corpus-trained SMILES policy
method_thesis: Train a compact autoregressive SMILES prior solely on the supplied unlabeled corpus, then initialize a fresh policy from that prior for each objective. Use the initial observations and each subsequent scored batch to update only its highest-reward sequences with the Augmented Hill-Climb loss: fit policy log likelihood to frozen-prior log likelihood plus scaled observed reward. Sample complete molecules token by token from the updated policy, canonicalize them, and refill invalid or duplicate proposals by further generation. The corpus supplies language training, never a ranked molecular pool. Elite-conditioned policy updates should shift generation toward new high-scoring molecular combinations quickly enough to improve the benchmark's mean final Top-1. This is a small-budget transfer hypothesis, not a claim that published larger-budget gains carry over. The root uses the current scored batch; randomized historical replay is reserved for the first improvement. The anchor's elite augmented-likelihood mechanism is described by [Thomas et al.](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13321-022-00646-z).

applicability_conditions: The Parent opportunity evidence is six appearances among 4,350 optimizer proposals, with original sampled-string and generation/learner provenance. The six appear in four sessions, are all nonelite and never improve an incumbent. Their recorded scores do not establish the scores of the Child's unseen replacements or the effects of later feedback.

R is the RDKit 2023.09.6 assignment of atom radical electrons on the parsed canonical emitted identity. It is an exact computational predicate under that representation, not an experimental measurement of spin state, reactivity, stability or synthetic feasibility. Other parser versions or chemical representations may assign unusual states differently.

The gate intentionally excludes all positive-R molecular identities, including cases where open-shell chemistry might be a legitimate scientific target. It therefore applies when exploration of closed-shell molecular identities is the desired coverage question; it is not a universal rule for every chemical task.

Closed-shell formal charges, zwitterionic atom charges, N-N/N-O bonds, sulfur and selenium are not prohibited. Ordinary nonradical but reactive handles, stereochemical ambiguity, unusual closed-shell valences, long linkers and excessive polar-group growth remain outside the mechanism.

No scalar score, objective identity, task name, seed, oracle budget or timeout enters the gate. Analysis may stratify the frozen panel by task and seed; the candidate remains task agnostic and all resources and the announced batch size remain protocol owned.

First-come comparisons reuse only the actual freshly generated stream and isolate immediate admission. Gate-induced refills can add later raw draws; changed accepted identities can change later policy states. Neither comparator nor surplus is an alternate scored Parent trajectory or retained candidate library.

The raw positive-R prevalence of the Parent's capacity-discarded draws is unknown. The observed generation surplus suggests replacement capacity but does not guarantee a closed-shell novel supply under later policy collapse. The inherited bounded failure remains visible, and diagnostic/inspection overhead must be reported.

The related sulfur-envelope gate n-93cd9a000278 changed chemical support with uneven scores, while halogen-attachment gate n-dfffb2c8d0b0 eliminated its targeted bonds but failed score non-inferiority. Neither tested radical-electron exclusion. Their results motivate a separate score-utility falsifier and prohibit equating a cleaner declared descriptor with better optimization.

The rejected core-thinning sibling n-33f9aab34e21 already shows that fresh-draw admission can alter later feedback and dilute useful exploitation. This rule preserves all core eligibility and does not promise higher diversity or a score gain. Preintervention matched controls and actual replacement receipts separate mechanical execution from those possible downstream effects.

approach.method_basis: The Parent trains a recurrent SMILES language model on an unlabeled molecular corpus and starts each objective with a policy copied from its frozen prior. It learns from the highest-scoring half of each accepted batch and the strongest eligible historical records in a memory of thirty-two elites. Original accepted strings and rewards are retained. Historical fitting weights diminish with previous exposure, while total current and historical loss shares stay fixed. Targets are prior sequence log likelihood plus sixty times reward, with individually positive targets capped at zero. Up to twelve clipped Adam steps minimize weighted squared residuals, retaining the final policy. Complete strings are sampled directly from that policy; RDKit validity and canonical novelty checks admit the first eligible molecules and refill the announced batch.
approach.novelty: Add one electronic-state admission rule: a sampled molecule must have zero RDKit-assigned radical electrons. A positive count redirects its slot to another fresh policy draw without editing atoms, charges, bonds or the sampled serialization. The earlier sampling child spaced repeated cores and lost endpoint score; this rule places no penalty on repeated cores. Earlier chemical gates in other lineages constrained sulfur environments or halogen attachments. This predicate instead checks the assigned unpaired-electron count on every element, leaving closed-shell charged species and ordinary sulfur chemistry eligible. The Parent's six observed cases establish a small but real opportunity. The claim is cleaner admitted electronic states with score non-inferiority, not a predicted endpoint increase.

research_intent.falsifier: The mechanism is refuted if an open-capacity valid canonical-novel row with recomputed R>0 is emitted, an R==0 row is vetoed by this gate, the logged radical sum disagrees with the parsed canonical atom states, or admission depends on charge, element identity, score or another undeclared predicate. If eligible positive-R opportunities occur but no actual closed-shell replacements reach a completed batch, delivery is unsupported; no eligible opportunities makes activation untested. Any molecular repair, accepted raw-string mismatch, gate-rejected identity entering global exclusions or learning, use of stored surplus as fallback, or mutation of frozen upstream logic violates the intended isolation. Count-partition failures or diagnostic changes to RNG/token draws also contradict the bound implementation. The proposed score utility is rejected if complete paired macro final Top-1 falls more than 0.002 below the Parent, using the protocol-supplied margin; a generation or resource failure prevents a successful non-inferiority claim. No endpoint increase, continued raw radical draws, or remaining nonradical reactive chemistry does not refute the registered electronic-state gate.

finding_summary.headline: Radical-bearing emissions fell to zero, but six replacements failed score non-inferiority.
finding_summary.insights:
Rare admission changes can matter even when the excluded parent molecules were poor and never selected for training. All eleven sessions without an open-capacity gate intervention reproduced the complete parent molecular and score sequence. Every affected session preserved its matched proposal prefix until the first rejection. One affected deco_hop session changed only two batches’ admissions and ordering: its selected training records and audited training quantities remained exactly equal throughout. In two other sessions, replacements entered the unchanged elite-selection rule, giving a direct route into later feedback. The same immediate chemical exclusion can therefore leave learning unchanged or alter it, depending on what fills the slot.

The largest loss followed a replacement that never trained. In its first affected zaleplon_mpo update, the ten selected training records, rewards and targets were identical to the parent, but the inherited padding width shrank from 72 to 60 tokens because it is set using the larger batch, including unselected strings. Tiny recorded update differences appeared immediately; a further proposal difference appeared in batch five, followed by broad trajectory divergence. This exposes a route for an unselected molecule to affect numerical execution and makes numerical sensitivity a plausible contributor to the loss. The logs do not isolate a hardware arithmetic cause or show that the radical-bearing chemical feature itself was useful. The evidence rules out treating “never elite” as sufficient assurance that rejection will preserve the later search.

The molecular assessment helps explain what this narrow predicate leaves open. The main losing trajectory explored many more long hydrocarbon appendages and failed to recover its parent’s compact heteroaryl-ether amide endpoint, whereas the improving trajectory favored less overdecorated anilinoquinazolines. These are observed chemical associations, not proof of a causal feature. Ring-rich exploration remains broad, while undefined stereochemistry, reactive closed-shell handles and uncontrolled appendage growth persist. Zero RDKit radical electrons therefore establishes the intended representation constraint, not general medicinal quality or stability. Future attempts would need to resolve replacement usefulness and sensitivity to batch representation; the present result does not support a score-safe blanket exclusion or a reduction in raw generation of unusual states.
finding_summary.results:
The electronic-state gate executed correctly. Across all three seeds and five tasks, it rejected six valid, novel, positive-radical draws while capacity was open and delivered six newly drawn closed-shell replacements. Those interventions occurred in six of 435 batches, spanning four task/seed sessions. Emitted positive-radical occurrence fell from the parent’s six in 4,350 proposals to zero in 4,350; the passive first-come comparator on the child’s actual stream also contained six. All 4,350 eligible zero-radical rows passed, including 315 charged molecules and 1,058 sulfur-containing molecules. Seventeen positive-radical raw-valid draws still occurred: six were rejected and eleven arrived after capacity was full. Thus admission changed; reduced raw radical generation has not been established. All 15 sessions completed their 300-evaluation budgets.

The promised score non-inferiority was rejected. Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.522705 to 0.516739, a paired change of −0.005966, exceeding the allowed 0.002 loss. Seeds 0 and 1 were unchanged; seed 2 lost 0.017898 in macro score. In that seed, zaleplon_mpo fell from 0.500000 to 0.391286, outweighing deco_hop’s rise from 0.666949 to 0.686174; the other three endpoints were unchanged. Population seed SD was 0.011993 versus 0.020072, and recorded mean AUC fell from 0.405593 to 0.404156. None of the six immediate replacements improved an incumbent; two entered subsequent real training. Total suggestion time rose from 24.745 to 31.427 seconds, including 6.185 seconds of inspection and 0.792 seconds in receipt regions. These are recorded regions, not isolated estimates of causal overhead.

finding_summary.headline: Radical-bearing emissions fell to zero, but six replacements failed score non-inferiority.
finding_summary.insights:
Rare admission changes can matter even when the excluded parent molecules were poor and never selected for training. All eleven sessions without an open-capacity gate intervention reproduced the complete parent molecular and score sequence. Every affected session preserved its matched proposal prefix until the first rejection. One affected deco_hop session changed only two batches’ admissions and ordering: its selected training records and audited training quantities remained exactly equal throughout. In two other sessions, replacements entered the unchanged elite-selection rule, giving a direct route into later feedback. The same immediate chemical exclusion can therefore leave learning unchanged or alter it, depending on what fills the slot.

The largest loss followed a replacement that never trained. In its first affected zaleplon_mpo update, the ten selected training records, rewards and targets were identical to the parent, but the inherited padding width shrank from 72 to 60 tokens because it is set using the larger batch, including unselected strings. Tiny recorded update differences appeared immediately; a further proposal difference appeared in batch five, followed by broad trajectory divergence. This exposes a route for an unselected molecule to affect numerical execution and makes numerical sensitivity a plausible contributor to the loss. The logs do not isolate a hardware arithmetic cause or show that the radical-bearing chemical feature itself was useful. The evidence rules out treating “never elite” as sufficient assurance that rejection will preserve the later search.

The molecular assessment helps explain what this narrow predicate leaves open. The main losing trajectory explored many more long hydrocarbon appendages and failed to recover its parent’s compact heteroaryl-ether amide endpoint, whereas the improving trajectory favored less overdecorated anilinoquinazolines. These are observed chemical associations, not proof of a causal feature. Ring-rich exploration remains broad, while undefined stereochemistry, reactive closed-shell handles and uncontrolled appendage growth persist. Zero RDKit radical electrons therefore establishes the intended representation constraint, not general medicinal quality or stability. Future attempts would need to resolve replacement usefulness and sensitivity to batch representation; the present result does not support a score-safe blanket exclusion or a reduction in raw generation of unusual states.

possible_failure_causes: Only the score-utility claim failed: the complete paired macro endpoint loss is 0.005965928693205336, beyond the supplied 0.002 margin. Mechanical exclusion and actual replacement delivery are confirmed.

Sparse opportunity limits immediate usefulness: six interventions among 4,350 intended outputs, no replacement incumbent gain and only two replacements selected for training. Excluding poor parent observations does not guarantee a useful or behavior-neutral replacement.

The largest regression follows a nonelite replacement that shrinks an inherited training tensor from 72 to 60 padded tokens despite identical selected records and targets. Immediate tiny logged update differences and later proposal divergence support numerical path sensitivity as a possible contributor; no counterfactual numerical execution identifies a unique hardware cause.

Actual replacement selection changes later learning in two sessions, while the task with the main endpoint loss explores much more long-chain chemistry. These downstream associations do not establish that removing radical chemistry itself caused the loss or that any unsubmitted discarded structure would have rescued it.

The predicate leaves reactive closed-shell handles, stereochemical ambiguity, long appendages and polar-group overgrowth untouched. The supplied chemistry assessment therefore supports a narrow electronic-state improvement alongside unresolved molecular-quality limitations.

Inspection and receipts increase measured suggestion time even though downstream raw draw counts and refills decrease. The timing regions include inherited operations, so causal overhead and wall-time variability are not isolated; no batch or session failed.

applicability_conditions: Evidence covers the complete fixed three-seed/five-task panel, all 435 optimizer batches per side and unchanged protocol-owned resources. The mechanism_result concerns activation only; this report does not decide Anchor eligibility.

The electronic predicate is the RDKit 2023.09.6 radical-electron assignment on canonical valid identities. It is appropriate only where closed-shell representation support is desired and does not certify experimental spin state, stability, synthesis or medicinal quality.

Six open-capacity positive-R opportunities supply direct activation evidence; eleven other positive-R draws occurred after capacity was full and are not interventions. No opportunity occurred for positive-R duplicates. Sessions without a gate opportunity supply matched controls, not independent activation successes.

All eligible R==0 rows, including closed-shell charges and sulfur chemistry, remain admissible. Source inspection shows no element, charge, size, task, seed, score or budget predicate and no molecular repair; R>0 would also exclude legitimate open-shell targets.

Same-stream first-come comparisons isolate immediate admission on actual child draws. They are not separately run parent policies or scored counterfactual trajectories. Only real accepted proposals, including actual replacements, are joined to observed scores; no discarded identity is assigned an invented outcome.

All 15 loaded priors and preintervention controls match. Parent full raw token tensors and discarded strings were not logged, so their raw radical prevalence cannot be compared, and reduced emitted prevalence cannot be promoted to a raw-generation-quality claim.

Frozen learning algorithms do not imply frozen behavior after feedback changes. Current-batch string lengths affect inherited padded training shape even when the changed record is not selected; recorded numerical-path differences remain distinct from a proven chemical cause of endpoint changes.

No gate-specific extra sampling call was needed in any active batch. Completion under this sparse panel does not guarantee future closed-shell supply under policy collapse; the inherited bounded failure remains present with no relaxed gate or stored surplus fallback.

All six rejected identities are absent from actual accepted feedback/training, and source placement keeps them out of pending/global exclusions. Within-suggestion deduplication remains inherited; no claim is made that an unobserved later repeat of a rejected identity was empirically tested.

The molecular report supports descriptive associations: the major loss accompanies excessive chain growth and the gain accompanies more compact decorations. Broad ring/core output and remaining undefined stereochemistry/reactive handles preclude a universal diversity, stability or medicinal-quality claim.

finding_summary.headline: Radical-bearing emissions fell to zero, but six replacements failed score non-inferiority.
finding_summary.insights:
Rare admission changes can matter even when the excluded parent molecules were poor and never selected for training. All eleven sessions without an open-capacity gate intervention reproduced the complete parent molecular and score sequence. Every affected session preserved its matched proposal prefix until the first rejection. One affected deco_hop session changed only two batches’ admissions and ordering: its selected training records and audited training quantities remained exactly equal throughout. In two other sessions, replacements entered the unchanged elite-selection rule, giving a direct route into later feedback. The same immediate chemical exclusion can therefore leave learning unchanged or alter it, depending on what fills the slot.

The largest loss followed a replacement that never trained. In its first affected zaleplon_mpo update, the ten selected training records, rewards and targets were identical to the parent, but the inherited padding width shrank from 72 to 60 tokens because it is set using the larger batch, including unselected strings. Tiny recorded update differences appeared immediately; a further proposal difference appeared in batch five, followed by broad trajectory divergence. This exposes a route for an unselected molecule to affect numerical execution and makes numerical sensitivity a plausible contributor to the loss. The logs do not isolate a hardware arithmetic cause or show that the radical-bearing chemical feature itself was useful. The evidence rules out treating “never elite” as sufficient assurance that rejection will preserve the later search.

The molecular assessment helps explain what this narrow predicate leaves open. The main losing trajectory explored many more long hydrocarbon appendages and failed to recover its parent’s compact heteroaryl-ether amide endpoint, whereas the improving trajectory favored less overdecorated anilinoquinazolines. These are observed chemical associations, not proof of a causal feature. Ring-rich exploration remains broad, while undefined stereochemistry, reactive closed-shell handles and uncontrolled appendage growth persist. Zero RDKit radical electrons therefore establishes the intended representation constraint, not general medicinal quality or stability. Future attempts would need to resolve replacement usefulness and sensitivity to batch representation; the present result does not support a score-safe blanket exclusion or a reduction in raw generation of unusual states.
finding_summary.results:
The electronic-state gate executed correctly. Across all three seeds and five tasks, it rejected six valid, novel, positive-radical draws while capacity was open and delivered six newly drawn closed-shell replacements. Those interventions occurred in six of 435 batches, spanning four task/seed sessions. Emitted positive-radical occurrence fell from the parent’s six in 4,350 proposals to zero in 4,350; the passive first-come comparator on the child’s actual stream also contained six. All 4,350 eligible zero-radical rows passed, including 315 charged molecules and 1,058 sulfur-containing molecules. Seventeen positive-radical raw-valid draws still occurred: six were rejected and eleven arrived after capacity was full. Thus admission changed; reduced raw radical generation has not been established. All 15 sessions completed their 300-evaluation budgets.

The promised score non-inferiority was rejected. Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.522705 to 0.516739, a paired change of −0.005966, exceeding the allowed 0.002 loss. Seeds 0 and 1 were unchanged; seed 2 lost 0.017898 in macro score. In that seed, zaleplon_mpo fell from 0.500000 to 0.391286, outweighing deco_hop’s rise from 0.666949 to 0.686174; the other three endpoints were unchanged. Population seed SD was 0.011993 versus 0.020072, and recorded mean AUC fell from 0.405593 to 0.404156. None of the six immediate replacements improved an incumbent; two entered subsequent real training. Total suggestion time rose from 24.745 to 31.427 seconds, including 6.185 seconds of inspection and 0.792 seconds in receipt regions. These are recorded regions, not isolated estimates of causal overhead.

molecular_assessment.headline: Ring-rich medicinal scaffolds with closed-shell atom assignments, but undefined stereochemistry, fragile handles and uneven appendage growth.
molecular_assessment.overall_character: The complete seeds 0, 1 and 2 were read for every objective in the supplied order; tasks_without_trajectories is empty. Each task contributes 900 accepted records, including 870 optimizer appearances. The digest initial excerpt shows seed 0 and its final excerpt shows seed 2; those excerpts are not the whole seed panel. All Child and Parent trajectory files were inspected passively. Across 4,350 Child optimizer appearances, RDKit 2023.09.6 perceives a median of 26 heavy atoms and three rings, with a heavy-atom range of 4 to 90. The digest ring-closure rates run from 0.9805 to 0.9977 and aromatic-text occurrence rates from 0.9460 to 0.9966; these are fractions of SMILES containing those features, not fractions of atoms that are aromatic. Aromatic amides, quinazolines, piperazines and other cyclic amines, sulfones/sulfonamides, ethers and halogenated aryl groups are prominent. Nonaromatic rings occur in 1,841 appearances, so this is not exclusively flat aromatic chemistry. The medicinal motifs make many individual structures apparently makeable, but the whole output also contains overgrown chains, repeated polar groups and reactive or form-sensitive attachments. That supports questionable synthetic plausibility and moderate drug-likeness for the collection, without asserting a synthetic route or experimental property. The 2,811 distinct nonempty atom/bond-typed Murcko cores indicate broad overall graph exploration; enrichment of the strongest molecules in narrower families remains visible. Core counts retain linker and heteroatom distinctions and do not measure diversity of biological activity. The Child has zero positive RDKit radical-electron assignments versus six Parent appearances, while 315 Child appearances contain formal atomic charges and 1,058 contain sulfur. This is a molecular-representation observation only. All tasks have a stereocentre-text rate of 0.0; passive perception nevertheless finds 870 Child appearances with at least one unassigned carbon stereocentre, and no explicit tetrahedral or bond-stereochemical text. Eleven complete task/seed molecular-score sequences match the Parent exactly; four differ, with unchanged endpoint identities in two of those. No mechanism-activation or score-utility decision is made. The reproducible passive counts, digest-to-trajectory checks, file hashes and per-seed comparisons are in r0012-08-improve-L03-molecular.audit.py and r0012-08-improve-L03-molecular.audit.json beside this report.

per_task.generated_character: Mostly medium-sized aromatic amides: optimizer heavy atoms have median 24 and range 4-90, with median three rings. The ring/aromatic text rates are 0.9908/0.9839. The strongest digest structure, O=C(NCc1ccccn1)c1cccc(Cn2ccccc2=O)c1, is a three-ring benzamide joining a pyridylmethyl group and an N-substituted pyridone. Other strong molecules include acetamido-indole carboxamides, anilinopyridine carboxamides, sulfinamides and an O-benzyl hydroxamate. These are recognizable medicinal motifs, although their exact molecular forms and synthesis have not been demonstrated. Seed 0 retains the indole-amide endpoint at 0.43351949803907636 and seed 1 the pyridone-containing benzamide at 0.4767312946227961. Both full streams match the Parent. That Parent structure is described from its trajectory rather than quoted because it is absent from this digest. The Child contains a much larger long-chain tail: 15 optimizer strings have an uninterrupted C run of at least 10, versus one in the Parent.
liabilities: Long hydrocarbon tails inflate size and flexibility; the worst set includes a very long-chain sulfonium species as well as long neutral amides. Closed-shell atom assignments do not resolve these liabilities.

The high-scoring sulfinamide/imidic-acid representations and hydroxamate show unresolved form-sensitive chemistry. Their presence is not evidence that all such bonds are unstable or synthetically inaccessible.
missing_features: Reliable retention of compact aryl/heteroaryl carbonyl arrangements during appendage changes is missing from much of the stream, especially the seed-2 long-chain excursion. The examples do not identify a unique absent target scaffold.

Defined configurations are missing for eligible stereogenic variants: 118 optimizer appearances have an unassigned carbon centre. Their scores do not establish that configuration assignment alone would improve this objective.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every task has a digest stereocentre-text rate of 0.0. transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator would need to recognize eligible stereogenic elements and generate explicit configurations while preserving connectivity and useful attachment relationships. Configuration coverage should be demonstrated on actual emitted identities; these records do not establish a score benefit for any stereoisomer.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The digest includes zero-scoring long-chain amides and peptide-like repeats. CCCCCCCCCC(=O)Nc1ccc(C(=O)Nc2cccc(F)c2)cc1 scores 0.000005647693002104746, whereas its shorter branched-acyl relatives score much higher. Conversely, useful molecules already include ordinary extended alkyl linkers. The full proposal panel spans 4-90 heavy atoms; extreme size is an observed output property, not a required property of its better structures.
transferable_gaps.gap: Appendage growth is not reliably coordinated with the existing scaffold and polar-group load.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The generator needs scaffold-context-dependent control of linker length, substituent extent and repeated polar functions while retaining learned attachment patterns. This evidence supports coherent growth from observed feedback, not a universal preference for short, nonpolar or minimally substituted molecules.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Strong emitted families include unacylated aryl/benzyl piperazines and linked cyclic amines, while a ring-N-acylated piperidine carboxamide is near the low end of its own observed score span. The full output already contains 1,003 appearances of an unacylated saturated ring-nitrogen proxy; there is no general absence of that chemistry.

Preserve or deliberately vary the role learned from accepted molecules instead of treating nitrogen count, ring presence or a universally basic piperazine as the objective.

transferable_gaps.evidence: All 4,350 emitted optimizer appearances have zero RDKit-assigned radical electrons, but Fc1ccc(N2CCN(CCCCNCc3ccc(OCCl)cc3)CC2)cc1F still scores 0.9999994163676008 and contains a chloromethyl ether. O=S(Nc1cc(C(O)=NCc2ccccc2Cl)ccn1)c1ccccc1 retains imidic-acid/sulfinamide form sensitivity at 0.42730032301881693. Other strong molecules contain ordinary sulfur chemistry or an N-O linkage, so a blanket heteroatom or bond ban would discard chemistry already associated with good observed values.
transferable_gaps.gap: Closed-shell atom assignments leave reactive attachment chemistry and uncertain molecular forms unresolved.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The generator needs context-aware treatment of electrophilic attachments and tautomer/ionization forms beyond parse validity and radical count. Any future change should distinguish a specific molecular-form concern from ordinary aryl halides, charges, sulfur or N-O chemistry, without equating a structural filter with demonstrated experimental stability.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The output has 2,811 nonempty atom/bond-typed Murcko cores, but all twelve highest entries in one digest are decorated anilinoquinazolines from a single seed. Another panel has 732 distinct typed cores while its strongest structure is an organized bis-sulfonyl piperazine. Thus neither complete scaffold collapse nor a general lack of rings explains the remaining chemistry; many different graphs are available but useful combinations are uneven.
transferable_gaps.gap: Broad graph novelty has not established reliable diversification of the attachment patterns in the strongest families.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The generator needs to explore altered ring topology, saturation and substituent vectors while retaining the functional-group relationships supported by its own accepted molecules. Evidence should track actual productive structural families, since additional canonical identities or core counts alone do not establish better chemistry.

possible_failure_causes: Only the score-utility claim failed: the complete paired macro endpoint loss is 0.005965928693205336, beyond the supplied 0.002 margin. Mechanical exclusion and actual replacement delivery are confirmed.

Sparse opportunity limits immediate usefulness: six interventions among 4,350 intended outputs, no replacement incumbent gain and only two replacements selected for training. Excluding poor parent observations does not guarantee a useful or behavior-neutral replacement.

The largest regression follows a nonelite replacement that shrinks an inherited training tensor from 72 to 60 padded tokens despite identical selected records and targets. Immediate tiny logged update differences and later proposal divergence support numerical path sensitivity as a possible contributor; no counterfactual numerical execution identifies a unique hardware cause.

Actual replacement selection changes later learning in two sessions, while the task with the main endpoint loss explores much more long-chain chemistry. These downstream associations do not establish that removing radical chemistry itself caused the loss or that any unsubmitted discarded structure would have rescued it.

The predicate leaves reactive closed-shell handles, stereochemical ambiguity, long appendages and polar-group overgrowth untouched. The supplied chemistry assessment therefore supports a narrow electronic-state improvement alongside unresolved molecular-quality limitations.

Inspection and receipts increase measured suggestion time even though downstream raw draw counts and refills decrease. The timing regions include inherited operations, so causal overhead and wall-time variability are not isolated; no batch or session failed.

applicability_conditions: The Parent opportunity evidence is six appearances among 4,350 optimizer proposals, with original sampled-string and generation/learner provenance. The six appear in four sessions, are all nonelite and never improve an incumbent. Their recorded scores do not establish the scores of the Child's unseen replacements or the effects of later feedback.

R is the RDKit 2023.09.6 assignment of atom radical electrons on the parsed canonical emitted identity. It is an exact computational predicate under that representation, not an experimental measurement of spin state, reactivity, stability or synthetic feasibility. Other parser versions or chemical representations may assign unusual states differently.

The gate intentionally excludes all positive-R molecular identities, including cases where open-shell chemistry might be a legitimate scientific target. It therefore applies when exploration of closed-shell molecular identities is the desired coverage question; it is not a universal rule for every chemical task.

Closed-shell formal charges, zwitterionic atom charges, N-N/N-O bonds, sulfur and selenium are not prohibited. Ordinary nonradical but reactive handles, stereochemical ambiguity, unusual closed-shell valences, long linkers and excessive polar-group growth remain outside the mechanism.

No scalar score, objective identity, task name, seed, oracle budget or timeout enters the gate. Analysis may stratify the frozen panel by task and seed; the candidate remains task agnostic and all resources and the announced batch size remain protocol owned.

First-come comparisons reuse only the actual freshly generated stream and isolate immediate admission. Gate-induced refills can add later raw draws; changed accepted identities can change later policy states. Neither comparator nor surplus is an alternate scored Parent trajectory or retained candidate library.

The raw positive-R prevalence of the Parent's capacity-discarded draws is unknown. The observed generation surplus suggests replacement capacity but does not guarantee a closed-shell novel supply under later policy collapse. The inherited bounded failure remains visible, and diagnostic/inspection overhead must be reported.

The related sulfur-envelope gate n-93cd9a000278 changed chemical support with uneven scores, while halogen-attachment gate n-dfffb2c8d0b0 eliminated its targeted bonds but failed score non-inferiority. Neither tested radical-electron exclusion. Their results motivate a separate score-utility falsifier and prohibit equating a cleaner declared descriptor with better optimization.

The rejected core-thinning sibling n-33f9aab34e21 already shows that fresh-draw admission can alter later feedback and dilute useful exploitation. This rule preserves all core eligibility and does not promise higher diversity or a score gain. Preintervention matched controls and actual replacement receipts separate mechanical execution from those possible downstream effects.

approach.method_basis: The Parent trains a recurrent SMILES language model on an unlabeled molecular corpus and starts each objective with a policy copied from its frozen prior. It learns from the highest-scoring half of each accepted batch and the strongest eligible historical records in a memory of thirty-two elites. Original accepted strings and rewards are retained. Historical fitting weights diminish with previous exposure, while total current and historical loss shares stay fixed. Targets are prior sequence log likelihood plus sixty times reward, with individually positive targets capped at zero. Up to twelve clipped Adam steps minimize weighted squared residuals, retaining the final policy. Complete strings are sampled directly from that policy; RDKit validity and canonical novelty checks admit the first eligible molecules and refill the announced batch.
approach.novelty: Add one electronic-state admission rule: a sampled molecule must have zero RDKit-assigned radical electrons. A positive count redirects its slot to another fresh policy draw without editing atoms, charges, bonds or the sampled serialization. The earlier sampling child spaced repeated cores and lost endpoint score; this rule places no penalty on repeated cores. Earlier chemical gates in other lineages constrained sulfur environments or halogen attachments. This predicate instead checks the assigned unpaired-electron count on every element, leaving closed-shell charged species and ordinary sulfur chemistry eligible. The Parent's six observed cases establish a small but real opportunity. The claim is cleaner admitted electronic states with score non-inferiority, not a predicted endpoint increase.

research_intent.falsifier: The mechanism is refuted if an open-capacity valid canonical-novel row with recomputed R>0 is emitted, an R==0 row is vetoed by this gate, the logged radical sum disagrees with the parsed canonical atom states, or admission depends on charge, element identity, score or another undeclared predicate. If eligible positive-R opportunities occur but no actual closed-shell replacements reach a completed batch, delivery is unsupported; no eligible opportunities makes activation untested. Any molecular repair, accepted raw-string mismatch, gate-rejected identity entering global exclusions or learning, use of stored surplus as fallback, or mutation of frozen upstream logic violates the intended isolation. Count-partition failures or diagnostic changes to RNG/token draws also contradict the bound implementation. The proposed score utility is rejected if complete paired macro final Top-1 falls more than 0.002 below the Parent, using the protocol-supplied margin; a generation or resource failure prevents a successful non-inferiority claim. No endpoint increase, continued raw radical draws, or remaining nonradical reactive chemistry does not refute the registered electronic-state gate.
research_intent.implementation_change:
Change only policy_sampling_admission. Keep sample_sequences' model calls, categorical probabilities, tensor shapes, token choices, EOS handling and returned tuple interface unchanged. Add passive receipts from the already sampled token tensor, including generation call, sample row, policy feedback version, exact token IDs through EOS or the full unterminated row, and its decoded raw or partial string. These receipts must consume no RNG and make no policy forward calls.

Add a pure inspection helper used inside suggest, leaving canonicalize and all ingestion, preparation, memory and adaptation code unchanged. For each RDKit-valid draw, parse the canonical isomeric identity returned by the inherited canonicalizer and compute R as the integer sum of atom.GetNumRadicalElectrons(). Record R and the contributing atom indices, atomic numbers, formal charges, degree and total valence. Also record charged-atom and sulfur-atom counts as passive controls. The gate is exactly R == 0 and does not use an element list, formal charge, sulfur envelope, substructure blacklist, molecular size, score, task identity, prior frequency or core multiplicity. Maintain a passive first-come comparator containing the first announced-count valid canonical-novel identities in the actual suggestion draw stream under its starting global exclusions and canonical deduplication, with this gate disabled.
